This release moves the built-in Dashboard into the standalone Dashboard Hub plugin and introduces deeper integration between the  two plugins.

## What’s new

  - Added integration with [Dashboard Hub](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-dashboard-hub).
  - LLM Hub now provides Dashboard Hub with configured AI models, chat handoff, Base generation, text rewriting, and workflow    generation and execution.

  - Dashboard Hub’s dashboard skill becomes available automatically when both plugins are enabled.
  - Added a read_timeline AI tool for retrieving Timeline activity by date.

### Important migration notice

  Dashboard functionality is no longer bundled with LLM Hub. To open existing .dashboard files or create new dashboards, install  and enable the separate Dashboard Hub plugin.

Existing dashboard files and data remain in your vault. The Create dashboard command is retained and delegates to Dashboard Hub  preserving existing hotkeys.

This release expands native web search beyond Gemini and introduces a unified search experience combining live web results with your vault
  context.

  ### Highlights

  - Added native web search for OpenAI, Anthropic, and Grok through their official APIs.
  - Web Search and Semantic Search (RAG) can now be enabled together.
  - Added inline citations and a deduplicated source list for web-search responses.
  - Search preferences are saved per workspace and reactivate automatically when returning to a compatible model.
  - Provider search metadata is preserved for compatible follow-up conversations.
  - Updated model listings, pricing estimates, documentation, and built-in help content.
  - Added comprehensive tests for provider web search, combined search behavior, workspace state, and chat history.

  Web search must be enabled from the search menu before sending a prompt. Availability depends on the selected provider and official API
  endpoint.

  ### Thanks

  Special thanks to [@melchoir55](https://github.com/melchoir55) for the major contribution in [#44](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-llm-
  hub/pull/44), bringing native OpenAI, Anthropic, and Grok web search together with RAG synthesis.

releases.description: # Dashboard A brand-new Dashboard view: build a personal home / overview page from a responsive grid of widgets. A dashboard is a plain .dashboard file you open like any note — live, editable, and synced with your vault. ✨ Highlights - Dashboard view — a responsive 12-column widget grid with view and edit modes. Drag to move, drag a corner to resize, configure via the gear, and add widgets from the palette. All edits save automatically; layouts reflow to a single column on narrow screens. - AI authoring — a built-in dashboard agent skill writes .dashboard files (and the backing .base files) from a chat prompt. releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
# Highlights

Multi-config Local LLM, two new pay-per-use OpenCode gateways, OpenCode local server framework, and native vault tools for tools-capable local models.

---
## ✨ Multi-Config Local LLM

Local LLM is now an array of configurations instead of a single entry. Each configuration:

- Has its own name, base URL, framework, optional Basic Auth, and multiple selected models.
- Surfaces in the chat dropdown as one entry per (config × model) combination — switch between Llama 3 on LM Studio, Qwen on vLLM, and Gemma on Ollama from a single dropdown.
- Has its own enable/disable toggle, verify state, and tools-rejection list.

Existing single-config setups migrate automatically into the new array form on first load — saved workspace state, discussion participants, and Discord conversations stay resolvable across the migration. No user action required. Two new pay-per-use OpenCode gateways and a new local LLM framework, plus native vault tool support for tools-capable local LLMs.

---
## ✨ New Providers

### OpenCode Zen / Go (Cloud API)

Both gateways are selectable from the API provider dropdown:

- OpenCode Zen — pay-per-use, includes free models (Big Pickle, MiniMax M2.5 Free, etc.) plus Claude, GPT-5.x, and more. Standard OpenAI-compatible /v1/models + /v1/chat/completions.
- OpenCode Go — $5 first month / $10/month subscription with curated coding models (GLM, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiMo, MiniMax, Qwen). 14-model fallback list is bundled because the API doesn't expose /v1/models.

### OpenCode (Local) Framework

Connect to a self-hosted opencode serve instance over its native session/SSE API. Supports macOS / Linux directly and Windows via WSL (with the documented OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD + --hostname 0.0.0.0 setup).

---
## 🛠️ Vault Tools for Local LLMs

Local LLMs running on LM Studio / vLLM / AnythingLLM can now use vault tools (read/write/search/edit) via OpenAI-style function calling — same UX as API providers, including all 15 vault tools, MCP, JS sandbox, and skill workflows/scripts.

- Default ON — first time you chat with a tools-capable model, function calling is attempted.
- Auto-fallback — if a model rejects the tools payload, it's flagged automatically and the chat falls back to the marker-based skill mode for that model. The flag persists, so subsequent turns skip the failed attempt entirely.
- Manual re-enable — clear the flag in Settings → Local LLM → Re-enable tools (e.g. after upgrading to a tools-capable build).
- Vault tool toggle in Chat now works for tools-capable Local LLMs (was previously locked to "off"). Choose All / No Search / None.

Note: Ollama and OpenCode (Local) frameworks still use marker mode only.
releases.name: v0.19.0

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
## Fixes

- Windows CLI: .cmd wrapper support without breaking existing settings. The plugin now runs the CLI through cmd.exe (shell: true) as a fallback so npm-generated gemini.cmd / claude.cmd / codex.cmd on PATH work out of the box — but only after failing to auto-locate the real .js entry point under %APPDATA%\npm\node_modules, %PROGRAMFILES%\nodejs\node_modules, or PATH-based node install directories. Claude's standalone installer at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\claude\claude.exe is also auto-detected again. Custom CLI paths dispatch by extension: .js → node <path>, .exe → direct, .cmd / .bat → shell. Existing Windows configurations pointing at ...\dist\index.js keep working unchanged, and prompts containing &, |, >, ^, %VAR% stay safe whenever a .js / .exe resolution is available (i.e. the common case).
- "Hide workspace folder" setting actually hides the folder again. Reverted to the body-class + hardcoded CSS selector approach used by the predecessor plugin. The previous inline-display: none implementation lost visibility whenever Obsidian's file explorer re-rendered its tree (on file create/rename/move), so the folder would flash back on every vault change. Now a single body class toggle and a CSS rule (body.llm-hub-hide-workspace-folder .nav-folder[data-path="LLMHub"]) survives any re-render. Limitation unchanged from the original: only hides the default LLMHub folder name.

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
✨ New features

- 1 file = 1 workflow: Each `.md` file now holds exactly one workflow code block. The Workflow panel drops the in-file dropdown and uses the filename as the workflow's display name everywhere (hotkeys, event triggers, sub-workflow refs, skill capabilities). This makes it possible to refer to a workflow by its file path alone — no more `path#name` IDs or guessing which block within a file is "the" workflow.
- Split into individual files migration: Open a legacy file that still has multiple workflow blocks and the panel shows a Split into individual files button. Clicking it writes blocks 2..N to sibling files (basename derived from each block's YAML `name:`, with collision-avoiding `-2`, `-3` suffixes) and leaves block 1 in the original file.
- AI-create collision check: When generating a workflow with AI, the modal pre-validates the output path. If the target file already contains a workflow block, you get a Notice and the modal stays open so you can pick a different name — no more silent appending or suffixing.
- @mention paths with spaces / unicode / special characters: File paths in chat messages and AI workflow prompts now resolve correctly when they contain spaces (`@My Folder/Note Title.md`), unicode (`@メモ/日本語.md`), or regex-special characters (`@notes/a (v2)+.md`). Fixes a long-standing limitation where the regex `[\w/-]+\.md` and `[^\s@]+` silently dropped any path that didn't match its narrow character class.
- @mention to non-Markdown files (workflow side): `@workflows/foo.yaml`, `@config.json`, `@diagram.canvas` etc. resolve again in the AI workflow prompt — restoring pre-refactor behaviour where the lookup did `getAbstractFileByPath(token)` for arbitrary paths.

⚠️ 1-file-1-workflow migration

If you have files with multiple `workflow` blocks from earlier versions:
- The Workflow panel becomes read-only on those files and shows the Split button to migrate them into per-file siblings.
- Existing hotkeys / event triggers persisted as `path#name` are silently rewritten to bare paths on plugin load (the `name` portion is dropped; if you had multiple hotkeys for blocks within the same file, they collapse to one entry pointing at the file).
- Skill capabilities lose their per-entry `name:` field — the workflow tool ID is now derived from the path alone (`Code Review/workflows_run-lint`).
- Sub-workflow nodes drop the optional `name:` property — only `path` matters.

After migration:
- Hotkey / event trigger display names come from the filename, so rename your workflow files to whatever you'd like to see in the command palette.
- Skill capabilities, hotkeys, and event triggers that referenced the original multi-block file's path stay attached to the first workflow after splitting — re-point them at the new sibling files manually if needed.

🛠 Fixes

- Adjacent `@mention` paths no longer skip the second one: the old regex's `(?:\s|$)` boundary consumed the whitespace between `@a.md @b.md`, so only `@a.md` was resolved. Both now resolve.
- `@foo.md` is no longer wrongly extracted from `@foo.md/child`, `@foo.md_backup`, `@foo.md.backup`, `@foo.mdx` etc. — the whole `@token` must match a vault path exactly.
- `get_workflow_spec` chat tool accepts bare-name `nodeTypes` strings (`"command"` or `"command, http"`) — some LLMs emit these despite the schema declaring an array, and the previous handler silently returned the full spec.
- Vault skills in `vaultToolMode: none` chat sessions: `read_note` is kept available whenever any non-builtin skill is active, so the model can still fetch SKILL.md to discover workflow capabilities.
- `extractInputVariables` (used to keep `SKILL.md` capabilities `inputVariables` in sync) now excludes any `_`-prefixed variable name, matching the system-variable convention documented in the AI workflow spec.
- `extractCapabilitiesBlock` surfaces YAML parse errors via `console.warn` (once per skill), so a typo in your `skill-capabilities` fenced block is visible to skill authors instead of being silently ignored.
releases.name: v0.18.0

releases.author: github-actions[bot]
releases.description:
✨ New features

- get_workflow_spec chat tool: Lets the chat LLM look up the workflow node spec on demand. Makes it easier to ask questions about specific nodes (e.g. http, command) or debug workflow YAML errors inside chat.
- [READ_SKILL: skillName] marker (CLI / Local LLM): Agent skills installed in the vault now work in CLI and Local-LLM modes. When the LLM emits this marker, the SKILL.md body and references are sent back as a follow-up message (previously only API / Discord modes could do this).
- Lazy-loaded skill content: Vault skill bodies and references/ are no longer always baked into the system prompt. Workflow / script IDs, descriptions, and input variables still appear in the prompt so everything stays invokable, but the longer body text is only loaded when the LLM actually needs it — noticeably smaller prompts without losing capability (built-in skills remain fully inlined).

⚠️  SKILL.md format update

Vault skill workflow / script definitions now live in a skill-capabilities fenced YAML block inside SKILL.md body, not in frontmatter. Frontmatter is reduced to user-facing metadata (name, description).

New layout:

---
name: my-skill
description: Do X
---

```skill-capabilities
workflows:
  - path: workflows/do-x.md
    description: Run X flow
    inputVariables: [filePath, mode]
scripts:
  - path: scripts/check.sh
    description: Validate output
```

You are ... <instructions prose>

Why: Keeps frontmatter free of plugin-specific schema, makes SKILL.md body the natural source of workflow documentation for the LLM, and reflects the reality that the LLM must read SKILL.md to know what a skill can do (both discovery and invocation go through the single "read SKILL.md" step — the separate skillVersion gate planned earlier turned out to be redundant and was dropped before release).

Migration:
- Existing skills that declare workflows: / scripts: in frontmatter keep working. A one-time console warning per skill points at the migration.
- Any edit via "Create Skill with AI" / "Modify Skill with AI" / direct node edits automatically rewrites the file into the new layout.
- No manual action required unless you hand-author skills and want to silence the warning.

🛠 Fixes

- Vault skills in CLI / Local-LLM mode: the [READ_SKILL: name] agent-loop marker (added in 0.17.0) now correctly loads skill bodies in those modes, including on Windows/CRLF-authored SKILL.md files (regex is CRLF-tolerant).
- No phantom workflows on script-only skills: "Modify Skill with AI" now refuses rather than fabricating a workflows/workflow.md capability when the target skill has neither a declared workflow nor a workflow file on disk.
- Multi-workflow skills preserve sibling inputVariables on save — earlier code dropped them when rewriting the capability list.
- Consistent AI skill-generation prompt: the generation prompt now tells the LLM that the skill-capabilities block (not frontmatter) is where workflow IDs and inputVariables land.

The old "Create as skill" checkbox has been removed. - Create workflow with AI — automate a predefined series of steps - Create skill with AI — bundle instructions + workflows the chat assistant can call on demand (output locked to skills/{{name}}) ### Modify Skill with AI 🎉 New button appears when editing a SKILL.md. Rewrites the SKILL.md instructions body and the referenced workflow file as one unit. Frontmatter entries (name / description / workflows[].path/name/description) are preserved; shared multi-workflow files are resolved by the declared name. ### Agent loop for CLI and local LLMs [RUN_WORKFLOW] / [RUN_SCRIPT] markers previously ran once and were substituted into the displayed message — the model never saw the results. Now: - Up to 5 iterations per turn: execute → feed results back as a follow-up user message → continue - Uses the persistent Claude CLI session or Gemini/Codex --resume sessionId to keep context - Brings CLI and local-LLM skill workflows closer to parity with function-calling on API chat ### Confirm modal UX - SKILL.md instructions diff added — previously only the YAML was diffed, so AI rewrites of the body were invisible - Instructions and YAML are shown as independent diff sections, each with its own split/unified toggle - "(no changes)" placeholder when AI output matches the existing content exactly - "Your request" read-only header at the top of the modal so the user remembers what was asked - Additional-request textarea now starts empty; label renamed to "Additional request:" (was "Enter your full request:" with the prior request pre-filled) ### Self-healing generation On YAML parse failure, the modal now re-prompts the LLM up to 2 times with the specific parse error + previous output so the model can self-correct. If both repairs fail, the modal stays open with the raw response and error message so you can copy the prompt into a stronger external LLM. ### Surface local-LLM runtime errors LM Studio / llama.cpp report errors like context-length overflow as HTTP 200 with an error field in the SSE payload. Previously: silent empty response. Now: the actual server message is displayed as an error. ## 🐛 Fixes - Skill chips in chat are now clickable and open SKILL.md (built-in skills stay static) - Failed run_skill_workflow calls now show an "Open workflow" button + hint pointing at the Modify-with-AI + execution-history recovery path. releases.description:
## Persistent CLI Sessions

CLI backends (Gemini CLI / Claude CLI / Codex CLI) now maintain session state across messages within the same chat thread or workflow execution. Conversation context is no longer lost between messages.

Claude CLI: Uses --input-format stream-json to keep a single process alive. The process is spawned on the first message and subsequent messages are written to its stdin as JSON objects, eliminating per-message process startup cost. Multi-line prompts, code blocks, and Markdown structure are preserved through JSON string escaping.

Gemini CLI: Now supports session resumption via --resume latest. After the first message, subsequent messages automatically resume the most recent session and send only the latest user message instead of re-transmitting the full conversation history.

Codex CLI: Session ID management is now handled through PersistentCliSession, ensuring the session ID is reliably carried across messages within a chat thread.

### Session Lifecycle

- Chat: Created on first CLI message, reused within the thread, terminated on model/provider change, new chat, chat switch, or unmount
- Workflow: Shared across CLI nodes via ExecutionContext, terminated when the workflow completes (success, error, or abort)

## Fixes

- Workflow abort signal now propagates to CLI command nodes, preventing partial responses from being saved as successful results
- All model change paths (UI selection, slash commands, settings sync, post-slash-command restore) now properly terminate the persistent CLI session

Added HTTP CONNECT proxy support for corporate gateway environments.

Configure proxy URL and bypass list in Settings > Proxy.

  - All features: Chat, API verification, image generation, embeddings (model discovery & vector generation)

The integration test suite (src/core/proxyFetch.test.ts) includes a working HTTP CONNECT proxy server implementation that can serve  as a starting point for building your own proxy. It covers authentication, TLS tunneling, and multiple LLM API endpoint patterns.

releases.description:
## LLM Hub for Obsidian v0.8.3

**LLM Hub** is a new plugin forked from [Gemini Helper](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-gemini-helper) (v1.10.13). As the plugin
 grew to support many LLM providers beyond Gemini, it was split into two separate plugins:

- **[LLM Hub](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-llm-hub)** (this plugin) — Multi-provider LLM support, desktop only
- **[Gemini Helper](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-gemini-helper)** — Gemini-focused, mobile supported

---

### Multi-Provider LLM Support

Use any LLM provider — switch freely during chat. Supports **Gemini**, **OpenAI**, **Anthropic**, **OpenRouter**, **Grok**, **local
LLMs** (Ollama, LM Studio, vLLM), and **CLI backends** (Gemini CLI, Claude CLI, Codex CLI). Multiple providers can be configured
simultaneously.

### Local-Only RAG with Multiple Embedding Backends

- Per-RAG embedding settings (URL, API key, model, chunk size, overlap, topK)
- Supports Gemini Embedding, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, Ollama
- External pre-built index support via `externalIndexPath`
- RAG context injection works with all providers (not exclusive with vault tools/MCP)

### Multimodal RAG (gemini-embedding-2-preview)

Index and search images, PDFs, audio, and video files — not just text. Toggle `indexMultimodal` in RAG settings (Gemini native
embedding only).

### MCP Stdio Transport

Local MCP servers can now run via stdin/stdout in addition to HTTP. Support `npx`/`uvx`-based MCP servers directly from Obsidian.

### Other Changes

- Anthropic provider with extended thinking and tool use support
- Desktop only (for mobile, use [Gemini Helper](https://github.com/takeshy/obsidian-gemini-helper))
- Renamed view types and codeblock to avoid conflicts with other plugins
- Plugin icon changed to `brain-circuit`

### Bug Fixes

- `prompt-file` and `file-explorer` workflow nodes now correctly use the `title` property
- Documented `mcp` node `saveUiTo` property and `rag-sync` node properties
